observations.title: Scanner removed package identities for all eight dependency advisories
observations.technical_explanation: All eight OSV-scanner candidates have their package details removed from the explanation field, leaving only GHSA IDs and severity levels. This prevents precise reachability analysis for each advisory. However, the project architecture provides strong contextual evidence: the manifest declares js as dist/index.js (a webpack bundle), the package.json lists only handlebars and sillytavern-utils-lib as production dependencies (both at current versions), and the devDependencies are exclusively build and test tooling. The 301KB lockfile size reflects the large transitive dependency trees of these build tools. This pattern is consistent with advisories in dev-only dependencies that do not ship with the extension. Running npm audit would provide the specific package names needed for a definitive assessment.
observations.layman_explanation: The security scanner found eight dependency issues but did not include which specific packages were affected. Based on how this project is built and packaged, these are most likely issues in development tools that are not included in the final product users install. The project owner should run a dependency audit to see the exact packages and update them.
observations.developer_action: Run npm audit in the project to obtain specific package names and versions for each advisory, then update affected packages. Prioritize any that turn out to be production dependencies.

observations.title: Multiple dependency advisories are most likely in build-time dev tooling, not shipped to extension users
observations.technical_explanation: All eight advisories were assessed collectively. The project has only two production dependencies (handlebars ^4.7.8 and sillytavern-utils-lib ^1.0.65) and a large set of devDependencies for build tooling (babel, jest, webpack, sass, typescript, etc.). The shipped artifact is a webpack bundle (dist/index.js per manifest.json), meaning devDependencies and their transitive dependencies are not included in the extension users install. The scanner removed package details from the advisory explanations, and the supplied source context is truncated to the first 41 lines of a 301 KB lockfile, so exact package-to-advisory mapping cannot be confirmed. However, the project structure strongly indicates these advisories are in dev-only transitive dependencies with no runtime reachability for end users. Routine dependency updates are recommended as good hygiene but no immediate user-facing risk is evident.
observations.layman_explanation: The project has multiple known-vulnerable dependencies flagged by the scanner, but these are most likely in build-time tools that do not ship to end users. The developer should keep dependencies updated as routine maintenance.
observations.developer_action: Periodically run npm audit and npm update to keep dev tooling current; verify production dependencies handlebars and sillytavern-utils-lib are at non-vulnerable versions.

observations.title: All three advisories likely reside in dev-only transitive dependencies
observations.technical_explanation: The project has only two production dependencies (handlebars 4.7.8 and sillytavern-utils-lib) but extensive devDependencies including babel, jest, webpack, sass, and typescript. These build tools pull in large transitive trees that commonly contain advisories. Since the manifest ships only dist/index.js and dist/style.css, dev-only dependencies do not reach end users. The scanner removed specific package names, preventing per-advisory confirmation, but the overall project structure supports this conclusion.
observations.layman_explanation: All three flagged vulnerabilities are probably in tools the developer uses to build the extension, not in the extension code that users actually run. This means the security warnings, while worth fixing eventually, pose little risk to people using the extension.
observations.developer_action: Run npm audit fix or update devDependencies to their latest versions to clear the advisories. This improves supply-chain hygiene but is not urgent for user safety.
